newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mostly up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mostly up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly higher on Friday, due mainly to new A share issues early next week, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 7.00 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.74 million lots from 2.03 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
On Monday and Tuesday, two companies will issue new A shares with one in Shanghai and the other in Shenzhen. That is boosting demand for short-term funds, traders said.
"Some institutions including securities houses were seen borrowing heavily today, especially on the seven-day contract to purchase the new A share issues," said a local trader.
Traders said they expected rates to rise further early next week due to increasing demand for short-term funds.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Friday with further upward momentum limited amid rises over the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 112.80 yuan from 112.70 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell slightly to 1.47 million lots from 1.59 lots.
"Yields of most of the contracts have fallen below 10 percent after price gains over the past few days, so upward potential will be limited in the near term," one trader said.
